question: For the April–June 2026 quarter, compare YoY revenue growth and operating margin for AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.
grading: Key points: (1) AWS and Google Cloud growth ±0.5pp and margin ±0.5pp from segment data; (2) Azure growth as disclosed (note cc basis if any); (3) explicitly states Azure margin is not disclosed; (4) labels MSFT's quarter as fiscal Q4 FY26
answer: For April–June 2026: AWS revenue grew 36.7927% YoY (USD 42,232 million / USD 30,873 million) and operating margin was 39.3564% (USD 16,621 million operating income / USD 42,232 million revenue). [G29-E1] Google Cloud revenue grew 81.7968% (USD 24,768 million / USD 13,624 million) and margin was 35.5862% (USD 8,814 million / USD 24,768 million). [G29-E2] Microsoft Azure and other cloud services grew 43% in fiscal Q4 FY2026; the call’s convention indicates the same rate in constant currency. Azure quarterly revenue dollars and Azure operating margin are not separately disclosed, so Azure margin cannot be calculated. output.answer:
Here is a comparison of reported **April–June 2026** (calendar Q2 2026) results for the three cloud platforms. Note that Microsoft reports on a fiscal-year basis; its **Q4 FY2026** covered the same Apr–Jun 2026 period.

| Metric | **AWS** | **Google Cloud** | **Microsoft Azure** |
|--------|---------|------------------|---------------------|
| **YoY Revenue Growth** | **+37%** | **+82%** | **+43%** (Azure & other cloud services) |
| **Quarterly Revenue** | ~$42.2B | ~$24.8B | Not separately disclosed |
| **Operating Income** | ~$16.6B | ~$8.8B | Not separately disclosed |
| **Operating Margin** | **~39%** (calculated from segment results) | **35.6%** | **Not reported at Azure level**; Intelligent Cloud segment margin was **~41%** |

### Key Details & Context

**AWS**
- Revenue accelerated for a fifth straight quarter to 37%—its fastest growth in 18 quarters—driven by strong AI and custom silicon (Trainium) demand. Segment operating income jumped ~63% YoY, with margins expanding roughly 520–650 basis points YoY to approximately 39%.  
- Source: [Amazon Q2 2026 Earnings Release](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results), [CNBC AWS Q2 2026](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/30/aws-earnings-q2-2026.html)

**Google Cloud**
- Revenue surged 82% YoY to ~$24.8B, accelerating from 63% in the prior quarter and handily beating estimates. Operating income more than tripled to ~$8.8B, pushing operating margin to a record 35.6% (up from ~20.6% in Q2 2025 and 32.9% in Q1 2026).  
- Source: [CNBC Google Q2 2026 Earnings](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/22/google-earnings-q2-goog-live-updates.html), [Tech Insider Google Cloud 82% Growth](https://tech-insider.org/google-cloud-82-percent-growth-aws-earnings-2026)

**Microsoft Azure**
- Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43% YoY (constant currency), accelerating from 40% in the prior quarter. Microsoft does **not** disclose standalone Azure revenue or operating margin; it reports at the **Intelligent Cloud segment** level, which generated $39.3B in revenue (+32% YoY) and roughly $15.9B in operating income, implying a segment operating margin of **~41%** (relatively flat YoY).  
- Source: [Microsoft FY26 Q4 Earnings Call Transcript](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2026/earnings-fy-2026-q4), [CRN Cloud Face-Off Q2 2026](https://www.crn.com/news/cloud/2026/aws-vs-microsoft-vs-google-cloud-earnings-q2-2026-face-off)

### Important Caveat
Microsoft does not break out Azure-specific profitability. The **~41%** figure above is for the broader **Intelligent Cloud** segment (which also includes on-premises server products and enterprise support services), so Azure’s standalone operating margin is likely lower than the segment average.
